messages.subject: Re: The missing env error
parts:
What are you trying to achieve with printing a geom_point?

Assuming you want a scatter plot, the code should run like:
ggplot(data = dfName, aes(x =..., y = ...) +
 geom_point()

In addition, after you have specified the dataframe name, in aesthetics there is no need to specify the variable fully like you do model12$cluster.
ggplot(data = model12, aes ( x = cluseter, etc...

Regards,
Sergey Bushmanov

messages.subject: Re: The missing env error
parts:
On 7/3/2014 3:55 AM, Sergey Bushmanov wrote:
> What are you trying to achieve with printing a geom_point?
>
> Assuming you want a scatter plot, the code should run like:
> ggplot(data = dfName, aes(x =..., y = ...) +
> geom_point()
>
> In addition, after you have specified the dataframe name, in aesthetics
> there is no need to specify the variable fully like you do model12$cluster.
> ggplot(data = model12, aes ( x = cluseter, etc...
>
> Regards,
> Sergey Bushmanov

A few additional comments in addition to Sergey's good observations.

You can print a geom_point, though it is fairly likely not what you are
expecting. It is a textual summary of the mapped aesthetics and other
set parameters:

print(geom_point(size=2.5, aes(colour=factor(model12$cluster))))
## mapping: colour = factor(model12$cluster)
## geom_point: na.rm = FALSE, size = 2.5
## stat_identity:
## position_identity: (width = NULL, height = NULL)

I don't have a model12 object in my environment, but since I never
evaluate or plot it, that is fine.

As Sergey said, to make a plot you want to not specify the vector in the
aes call, but a reference to a column in a supplied data frame

ggplot(data=model12) +
geom_point(size=2.5, aes(colour=factor(cluster)))

This leads to my final point: is model12 a data.frame? ggplot works with
data in data.frame's. There are helper functions to get data in several
common format into a data.frame for use with ggplot (see the fortify
family of functions), but you need to know what each does to know what
variables are available to you.
